title: Inclusive lesson planning
assignment: Create an inclusive science lesson plan about falling objects. Explain how you would diagnose the misconception that heavier objects always fall faster, justify a teaching strategy for the learner, and adapt the assessment to a stated accessibility constraint. Students must demonstrate these decisions individually at the checkpoints.
ai_permissions: While preparing the lesson plan, GenAI may help draft activities and suggest resources. Students must disclose suggestions they use. During supervised checkpoints, no GenAI is permitted; students must independently diagnose the misconception, justify a teaching strategy, and adapt an assessment to the stated learner and classroom context.
budget_scope: Additional checkpoint work; existing product marking excluded

requirements.description: Justify a teaching strategy against that learner need.
Given an accessibility constraint, revise the assessment response format while preserving the learning outcome and success criteria; justify how the revision still elicits the required evidence.

checkpoints.name: Misconception response
checkpoints.prompt: A learner says, "Heavier objects always fall faster." Independently identify the misconception and write one question that would help reveal the learner's reasoning.
checkpoints.conditions: Complete this task individually during the supervised checkpoint, without GenAI. Identify the misconception in the learner's statement and propose a question that would help reveal the reasoning behind it.
checkpoints.ai_permissions: No GenAI during this supervised checkpoint. Students complete the response independently.
checkpoints.mapping_rationale: The response provides direct evidence for E1 because each student identifies the misconception and proposes a question to investigate the learner's reasoning. Do not use this checkpoint to score teaching-strategy selection or assessment adaptation.

approval.reviewer: Original development fixture; expert review pending

checkpoints.name: Individual strategy explanation
checkpoints.prompt: After diagnosing the learner's belief that heavier objects fall faster, select a teaching strategy for this learner. Explain how the strategy addresses the misconception and identify an observable learner response that would indicate understanding.
checkpoints.conditions: Complete this task individually during the supervised checkpoint, without GenAI. Select a strategy suited to the diagnosed learner need, explain how it addresses the misconception, and identify an observable response that would indicate understanding.
checkpoints.ai_permissions: No GenAI during this supervised checkpoint. Students complete the response independently.
checkpoints.mapping_rationale: This response provides direct evidence for E2 because each student selects and justifies a teaching strategy in relation to the learner's misconception. Score the fit and explanation of the strategy. Do not use this checkpoint to score misconception diagnosis or assessment adaptation.

approval.reviewer: Original development fixture; expert review pending

checkpoints.name: Adaptation with justification
checkpoints.prompt: During a supervised checkpoint, the standard printed worksheet is inaccessible to a learner with low vision. Propose an accessible response format for assessing the science learning outcome about falling objects. Explain why your alternative preserves the same outcome and success criteria and allows the learner to show what they understand.
checkpoints.conditions: Complete individually without GenAI. Name the accessibility constraint; specify the alternative response format; state the unchanged learning outcome and success criteria; explain how the alternative elicits evidence of understanding without changing what is assessed.
checkpoints.ai_permissions: No GenAI during this supervised checkpoint. Students complete the response independently.
checkpoints.mapping_rationale: This checkpoint directly supports E3: the student revises the assessment in response to a specified accessibility constraint and justifies how the revised format preserves the intended outcome and success criteria. Score accessibility fit and whether the revised format elicits the required evidence. Do not count this response toward E1 misconception diagnosis or E2 teaching-strategy justification.

approval.reviewer: Original development fixture; expert review pending

checkpoints.name: AI-use reflection
checkpoints.prompt: After preparing the lesson plan, identify one GenAI suggestion you used, adapted, or rejected. Explain your decision in relation to the learner and classroom context, and state how you documented the AI contribution. This reflection records the planning process; it is not evidence of independent performance on E1-E3.
checkpoints.conditions: Complete individually after lesson-plan preparation. Describe one specific AI suggestion and whether it was used, adapted, or rejected; explain the decision with reference to the learner/context. Do not treat this self-report as proof of authorship or as evidence that E1-E3 have been met.
checkpoints.ai_permissions: GenAI may be used during lesson-plan preparation as stated in the assignment rules. Do not use GenAI to draft or revise this reflection; disclose any planning suggestions used.
checkpoints.mapping_rationale: D is a context-only process record and has no evidence links. It documents reported AI use and the student's reasoning about a suggestion, but self-report does not establish authorship or independently demonstrate E1-E3. Do not count D toward any evidence requirement.

checkpoints.name: Combined supervised scenario
checkpoints.prompt: A: A learner says heavier objects always fall faster; identify what you would ask to diagnose the reasoning. C: Your planned assessment becomes inaccessible to a learner; propose an alternative and justify its fit to the outcome. E combines diagnosis, strategy and assessment revision in one unfamiliar case. Candidate: Combined supervised scenario.
checkpoints.conditions: E1 Diagnose an unfamiliar misconception. E2 Justify a teaching strategy against that learner need. E3 Revise assessment after a new classroom constraint. Each requires one individual demonstration; justify revisions using the stated context.
checkpoints.ai_permissions: Develop an inclusive lesson plan and justify its teaching and assessment decisions. GenAI may draft activities and suggest resources; disclose accepted suggestions. Checkpoints assessing independent performance allow no GenAI during delivery.
checkpoints.mapping_rationale: Score diagnosis, contextual justification and assessment fit separately. D and F provide context only. A fluent reflection cannot satisfy E1–E3 under the stipulated independent-performance conditions.
